# MainFrame

A terminal window that wraps the native Windows shell over ConPTY, built on the VexelRay stack.

## Install (Windows)

Open **PowerShell** (a normal window - administrator rights are not needed) and run:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/mainframe/install.ps1 | iex
```

That is the whole install. A window opens where you can change the folder and choose shortcuts,
PATH and file types, then press **Install**. It downloads MainFrame 0.1.1, checks every file
against the SHA-256 in the [install manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/mainframe/manifest.json), and installs for your user only.

What it does:

- creates the install folder and places the binaries there
- unblocks them and makes sure they are executable
- creates desktop / Start menu shortcuts
- adds the install folder to your user PATH
- writes an install manifest listing everything it installed and where
- adds an uninstaller and an updater next to the binaries, and an entry in Settings > Apps

### Options

The window covers the folder and the `NO_*` choices. For a scripted install, or one without the
window, set these in the same PowerShell window *before* the install command:

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `$env:INSTALL_VERSION = '1.2.3'` | install a specific version from the [history](#versions) |
| `$env:INSTALL_DIR = 'D:\Apps\MainFrame'` | install somewhere other than `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\MainFrame` |
| `$env:INSTALL_NO_SHORTCUTS = '1'` | skip the desktop / Start menu shortcuts |
| `$env:INSTALL_NO_PATH = '1'` | do not add anything to your user PATH |
| `$env:INSTALL_NO_ASSOCIATIONS = '1'` | do not register MainFrame to open any file types |
| `$env:INSTALL_FORCE = '1'` | reinstall even if this version is already installed |
| `$env:INSTALL_SKIP_CHECKS = '1'` | install even if this computer does not meet the system requirements |
| `$env:INSTALL_QUIET = '1'` | no window: ask nothing and report in PowerShell only |
| `$env:INSTALL_CLOSE_APPS = '1'` | close MainFrame if it is running and holds a file the update replaces |

Updates and reinstalls remember the `INSTALL_NO_*` choices of the last install. To get shortcuts,
the PATH entry or file types back, set that variable to `'0'` and run the install command again.

### What gets installed

| File | Kind | Version | Size | Installed to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mainframe.exe` | native executable | 0.1.1 | 43.1 MB | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\MainFrame\mainframe.exe` |
| `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` | file | 0.1.1 | 0.1 MB | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\MainFrame\THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` |

Everything installed is recorded in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\MainFrame\install-manifest.json`, and a copy
in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\vexelray-installer\installs\mainframe.json`.

### Other programs finding MainFrame

Installs are independent, so MainFrame can sit next to other programs from the same
installer. To start it from one of them without depending on PATH, read
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\vexelray-installer\installs\mainframe.json` and use `commands.<name>.path` - an absolute path to the
executable (the `.cmd` launcher for a jar). Missing file means not installed. Pass arguments
as usual; from Java use `new ProcessBuilder(path, args...)`, and for a `.cmd` launcher run it
as `cmd.exe /c path args...`.

### Update

Open **sibarum apps** from the Start menu. It lists everything installed this way, with **Update**,
**Change...** (folder, shortcuts, PATH, file types), **Remove** and **Update all**. Or update from PowerShell:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\MainFrame\update.cmd"
```

Checks GitHub for newer versions of the binaries and installs them after asking. Use
`-Check` to only look, `-Yes` to skip the question.

An update that fails or is interrupted puts back the version you had, exactly as it was. If the computer
went off halfway, the next install or update first finishes putting it back.

### Reporting a problem

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\MainFrame\diagnose.cmd"
```

Writes a report about this computer and prints where it is: Windows version, processor, memory, the displays
(resolution, refresh rate, scaling, HDR), each GPU as DXGI / Direct3D 12 and as Vulkan see it, whether a
flip-model swapchain can be created, the Vulkan present modes, implicit Vulkan layers, and what is installed.
Nothing is sent anywhere; your user name is replaced by `%USERPROFILE%`. Read it, then attach it to [your bug report](https://github.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/issues/new).
`-Copy` also puts it on the clipboard. Without installing, run `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/mainframe/diagnose.ps1 | iex`. A failed
install writes the same report by itself.

### Uninstall

Use **Settings > Apps > MainFrame > Uninstall**, or:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\MainFrame\uninstall.cmd"
```

The uninstaller reads the install manifests in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\vexelray-installer\installs`, so it removes exactly
what was installed - files, shortcuts, PATH entries, file types and the Apps entry. Files you added to
the install folder are left alone. `uninstall.cmd -List` shows every install it knows about
and `-All` removes them all.

### Is it safe to run a script from the internet?

Read it first - it is one file: [`install.ps1`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/mainframe/install.ps1). Downloads are only
accepted when their SHA-256 matches the manifest, and the manifest and script live in this
repository.

macOS and Linux installers are planned; the manifest is already organised per platform.

## Versions

Current version: **0.1.1**. The full history of published versions, with the files,
sizes and checksums of each, is in [`manifest.json`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sibarum/vexelray-dist/main/apps/mainframe/manifest.json).
